clue.text: Fanciful idler — he's well-liked

indicators.note: fanciful means imaginatively reworked, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: he's is a contraction of he is, giving its letters H, E, S

explanation.surface: Someone lazy but cheerful is popular all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fanciful' looks like a description of the idler, but it tells you to rearrange IDLER plus HES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relished is enjoyed with great pleasure, so it is much appreciated.

clue.text: Mac's a riot — can juggle

definitions.note: the 's here is short for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: to juggle is to shuffle things around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is great fun and can do a juggling act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' looks like a Scottish man, but it is short for mackintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a waterproof coat.

clue.text: Birds alight on the fence

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first word sits atop the second

parts.note: to land is to alight, come down
rails form a fence

explanation.surface: Birds coming to rest on a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Landrails are corncrakes, a kind of bird of meadows.

clue.text: Breezy point up country here

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: breezy means airy
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A windy spot in the uplands of this land.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: The origin of a waterfall?

parts.note: read 'waterfall' as a fall in the level of water, as when the sea retreats, rather than a cascade

explanation.surface: Where does a cascade begin?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a 'water fall' is the falling of the sea level.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding tide makes the sea level drop, so it causes the water to fall.

clue.text: Charming things, though they're not long-lasting

explanation.surface: Magic charms that wear off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spells are magical charms; spells are also brief periods of time, such as a spell of rain.

clue.text: Soft grain, inferior but still highly esteemed

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft
rice is a cereal grain
less means lesser, inferior

explanation.surface: Poor-quality mushy cereal that people still prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Something priceless is invaluable, beyond any price.

clue.text: Turner's given a trainee two different articles

definitions.note: the definition names the turner's machine; the 's here means has

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
a is the indefinite article and the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article and the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An apprentice gets a pair of grammatical items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but it is a woodworker or metalworker who shapes material on a rotating machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is the machine a turner uses to shape wood or metal while it spins.

clue.text: Issue a word of thanks for the music

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Saying thank you for the tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a classical composition for one or more instruments.

clue.text: One's after a fellow — a most presentable young man

indicators.note: after means the 'one's' piece follows the others

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
one is I, and 's stands for is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a man described as a handsome youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, so his name stands for any handsome young man.

clue.text: This will be seen all around the bull ring

definitions.text: This will be seen all around the bull ring

parts.words: This will be seen all around the bull ring
parts.note: on a dartboard or shooting target, the ring immediately surrounding the bull's-eye is given a name, not the arena of a bullfight

explanation.surface: Something visible on every side of a bullfighting arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull ring' suggests a bullfight arena, but the bull here is the bull's-eye of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target, the ring next to the central bull's-eye is called the inner.

clue.text: It's reprehensible to make money over a game

parts.note: reprehensible conduct is bad
to mint is to produce coins
on means over, as in resting on top of something

explanation.surface: Printing money for a sport is wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock.

clue.text: For state to pursue private transport would be a bloomer

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the state's word comes after the transport's

parts.note: a car is a private vehicle
a nation is a state

explanation.surface: A government chasing personal vehicles would be making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' sounds like a blunder, but here it is a flower: something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnation is a garden flower, and anything that flowers is a bloomer.

clue.text: Held by college lecturers due to take up appointments

indicators.note: held by signals that the answer is contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: University teaching staff are kept on until they take up new posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chosen for office who has not yet taken it up, as a president-elect, is described this way.

clue.text: Really stupid, like doubly trendy egghead

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as gold'

indicators.note: doubly means the word for trendy appears twice in succession

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
the head of the word egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: A fashionable intellectual is described as very foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it is read as the head (first letter) of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means as foolish as an ass, utterly silly.

clue.text: When idle it can break just the same

indicators.note: break means the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A machine left idle may fail in the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike.

clue.text: Provide excitement in extremely smooth, figure-hugging dress

indicators.note: in places the word for excitement inside the other letters
extremely means take only the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: heat is excitement or intensity, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A slinky, close-fitting outfit is said to cause a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting, straight dress.

clue.text: Worker trying to make good takes the blame first

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
1st is the abbreviation for first, read as IST

explanation.surface: An employee seeking to put things right accepts responsibility before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like a timing word, but it is 1ST with the one read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist works to heal or restore people, making them well.

clue.text: Someone not suited for running

parts.note: read 'not suited' as wearing no clothes rather than unfit, for a person dashing about

explanation.surface: A person ill-equipped to be a runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not suited' suggests unfit, but it means without a suit of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker runs naked through a public place.

clue.text: A track for climbers

parts.note: a scent is the trail or track followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A path laid out for mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: the way up a mountain is a track used by climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward route, the route mountaineers take.

clue.text: It's so lethargic — prod it to move

indicators.note: move signals the letters of prod it are shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something so sluggish you must poke it to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means sluggish and inactive.

clue.text: Check, and find crawler has pocketed money

indicators.note: has pocketed means the crawler's word swallows the money's letter

parts.note: an insect is a creeping creature
p is the abbreviation for penny or pence, a coin of money

explanation.surface: Examine things and discover that a sycophant has been taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests a toady, but here it is a creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely.

clue.text: Strained to get in double figures — the beginning of the end!

parts.note: tens are numbers in double figures

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Reaching double figures marks the start of the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means highly strained or concentrated.

clue.text: Commentaries for Tests

explanation.surface: Notes accompanying cricket matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tests' suggests Test matches in cricket, but here it means attempts or trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Essays are written discussions of a subject; to essay is also to try, so essays are attempts.

clue.text: Traps specially designed for small fish

indicators.note: specially designed signals that the letters of the word traps are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Purpose-built snares to catch little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small herring-like sea fish.

clue.text: Weapon of the Left in general

indicators.note: in puts the left's letter inside the word for general

parts.note: rife means widespread, general

explanation.surface: Arms carried by left-wingers generally.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun.

clue.text: To limit the drink makes good sense

parts.note: to ration is to limit the amount allowed
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Restricting alcohol is a sensible policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or logical basis behind something.

clue.text: Go round — otherwise a scrap will result

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'
a bit is a scrap or fragment

explanation.surface: Back off or a fight will break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight, but it is a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to circle around something.

clue.text: "And keep you in the rear of your ______" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: And keep you in the rear of your

parts.words: And keep you in the rear of your
parts.note: a line from Hamlet where Laertes warns Ophelia to hold back her feelings for Hamlet; the missing word completes the quotation

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Laertes, Act 1 Scene 3: 'And keep you in the rear of your affection, Out of the shot and danger of desire.'
explanation.definitionFit: The word completing Laertes' line means fondness or love, which Ophelia is told to keep in check.

clue.text: A person who can be relied on should never be dropped

definitions.text: A person who can be relied on

explanation.surface: Advice that a dependable friend must not be abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'drop a brick' is a British idiom for making a tactless blunder, so it is something you should never do.
explanation.definitionFit: A brick is an old-fashioned term for a loyal, dependable person; dropping a brick means committing a social gaffe.

clue.text: Very hard and slippery creature in a foul place

indicators.note: in tells us the creature sits within the foul place

parts.note: a sty is a filthy place, a pigsty
an eel is famously slippery

explanation.surface: A tough slimy animal found in a filthy spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and unyielding, like steel.

clue.text: The man willing to have a pot at gold

parts.note: a pot is a try or shot, so to have a pot is to test or try
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man ready to take a shot at winning gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' looks like eager, but it means making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so he is literally the one doing the willing.
